original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract outside the frozen catalogue whose per-call profile, screened with ceiling.ceiling(), beats the selected word's packing ceiling; a lower cap does not establish identical circuitry or order attainable optima, and is insufficient to pass the stronger-budget target under this model. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Packing of the selected word is capped at +0.87% (ceiling model); only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises the cap.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: On the actual PR2857 shared-kernel words used by the T185 frontier (#2863) and the newer PR2894 preload-move words, screen every remaining single-helper dirty entry (a changed helper inventory: one helper starts at a nonzero frame, losing width and its first climb, with its dirt cancelled in-program by inserted adds) under exact time-dependent responses and full-program frame feasibility, including partner cancellation, sub-frame entry, insertions in either phase and one-hop relays; plus, as a labelled side check, single-gate and cascade frame refits of the same words.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a new helper inventory beating packing. #2863 proved the fixed-inventory packing optimum, so the remaining lever is a changed native word. This package bounds the most direct inventory change (more dirty entries, the mechanism of #2833/#2853/#2857) on the frontier words instead of proposing a new contract. The frame-refit screens touch a scope-change trigger (monotone frames within a fixed word, #1995/#2013) and are reported only as a side check on these newer words.
bottleneck_link: Dual prices of the #2863 fixed packing model value one more PR2857-type width reduction at about +3.6e-7 kappa and entering at a dimension-1 first frame at about +5.9e-7 before receiver costs, against about 4e-9 for any packing move; a positive screen would be the cheapest record-scale lever. The negative result removes it in the screened class and shows the obstruction is frame placement, not algebra.
stop_rule: Stop when the calibrated screen (must reproduce exactly the 16 PR2853 quartet helpers on the PR2833 words) gives no frame-feasible single-helper entry on both current providers in every mode, and every apparent relay fails the exact bilinear validity test; any positive hit must be built literally and pass the exact zero-residual check before being reported.
evidence: verify.py --part core/chains (registered). PR2857 words: 0 of 184 eligible helpers in direct and pre-only modes (86 have a zero-frame first gate); 8 apparent one-hop relays, 0 valid; refits 0 improving (345 single-gate candidates, 2797 forward and 3009 backward cascades). Controls: PR2833 words give exactly the 16 quartet helpers; corrupted compensation and a broken frame chain are rejected; a de-optimised word is repaired by the refit screen; the relay validity test accepts known quartet relays; frames relaxed, 184/184 helpers are algebraically cancellable (evidence/RELAXED-CENSUS.json). PR2894 words: 0 of 182 eligible, 8 apparent relays and 0 valid, refits 0 improving; its two preload-move quartets are zero-frame-first in the PR2857 words (outside the fixed-gate class), consistent with the relaxed control. Independent #2863 fast and full cold replays: evidence/T185-REPLAY.json.
author: digitalis-p

Four screen bugs found during the session were fixed before publication and are described in README. No independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can the phase-A mixing block be re-routed so that some of the 86 zero-frame-first helpers start at nonzero frames without repaying the saving elsewhere?
open_questions.why_it_matters: With frames relaxed every one of the 184 eligible helpers is algebraically cancellable, so frame placement is the only obstruction found; each realised entry is worth roughly +1e-7 to +6e-7 kappa first-order. #2894 realises two such quartets by preload re-synthesis, leaving 84 on its words.
open_questions.first_step: Pick one zero-frame-first helper (e.g. 242), list the mixing-block gates that pin its first frame, and search for a reordering or frame change that admits a nonzero entry frame while keeping the exact endpoint audit (PR2833 audit_local.py) passing.
open_questions.blocked_by: Needs a changed mixing schedule plus its climb bill; the screen here keeps every existing gate frame fixed.

open_questions.question: Do simultaneous multi-helper entries or relations with two or more outside helpers (for example comp[479] in terms of helpers 502/503/490) admit a frame-feasible plan that single-helper screens cannot see?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This screen is single-helper and one-hop; joint plans can share receivers and frames. #2875 and Discussion #2612 also list this lane as unsearched.
open_questions.first_step: Extend tools/entry_screen.py to a joint span test for a pair of helpers with shared receivers and exact superposition checks, starting with the 479/481/491/493 relations.
open_questions.blocked_by: Overlaps the advisory structural investigation in Discussion #2612; coordinate before a construction round.

open_questions.question: Can operator-word (warp) corrections make the warp-tainted helpers cancellable?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Tainted helpers are excluded here because their responses are operator-valued.
open_questions.first_step: Reuse the initial_corrections operator-word contract from PR2226/PR2833 and test one tainted helper's response in the free algebra.
open_questions.blocked_by: Requires the free-operator replay of the inherited auditor, not only rational responses.
